method: Deterministic summary of computed figures. No language model is used.
national: One Nation led national search interest in the week to 15 October, averaging 21.4 on Google's 0-100 scale, 4.0 times the next party (the Greens). That is 62% of all search interest across the parties tracked.
The Greens rose the most on the previous week, up 1.0 points (+23%); One Nation fell furthest, down 7.6 points (-26%).

Searches for the Greens jumped to 18 on 15 October, 5.5 times the previous week's average. Coverage around that day: “Shoebridge says Greens taking allegations against senator 'incredibly seriously' — as it happened” (ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation).

Searches for One Nation jumped to 30 on 3 October, 2.0 times the previous week's average. Coverage around that day: “One Nation promises law-and-order boost in Victorian campaign launch” (ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation).
Fastest-rising searches alongside One Nation: “mike newman”, “mike newman one nation”, “one nation ai video”.
victoria: 41 days until Victorians vote on Saturday 28 November 2026.

Across the latest poll from each of 4 pollsters, the Coalition averages 29.2% of the primary vote, Labor 24.5%, One Nation 22.2% and the Greens 14.8%. On two-party-preferred the Coalition leads 53.7 to 46.3 (3 polls), an 8.7-point swing to the Coalition since 2022.
Applied uniformly to the 2022 pendulum, that swing points to a Coalition majority (50 seats, 45 needed). Treat this as the classic two-party read only: it cannot see One Nation winning seats.
The Roy Morgan MRP (March 2026 - September 2026), which models seats one by one, projects Coalition 62, Labor 40, One Nation 11 and Greens 6: a majority.
Preferred premier (Resolve, 6–10 Oct 2026): Wilson 29%, Carroll 22%, Pickering 14%.
